logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Enter the dashboard’s fullscreen mode and choose More info. No information dialog is visible until fullscreen is exited, when the already-open dialog appears; the button is not simply failing to receive the click.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The dashboard enters element fullscreen while the info UI is mounted through a portal outside that element. The browser only presents descendants of the fullscreen element, so the already-open dialog appears after fullscreen exits. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: In Metabase, a dashboard is a page of charts, tables and text. Enter its fullscreen mode and choose More info: no information dialog is visible. Exiting fullscreen reveals the already-open dialog, showing that the action ran but its result was hidden outside the fullscreen view.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. On the supplied dashboard, choose a single product category and inspect the Product breakdown card. It continues showing every category despite the dashboard’s advertised filter; the report concerns this seeded card’s missing connection rather than a newly authored card that has never been mapped.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashboard filtering applies only stored dashcard parameter_mappings. This card has no effective Product Category mapping in the seed; the application cannot infer a mapping from adjacent text or charts. Seed records need separate inspection. The exact cause remains unresolved. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On the supplied e-commerce dashboard, choose one product category in the dashboard filter, which should restrict its connected charts. The Product breakdown chart still includes every category even though surrounding text names the chosen one. This concerns the supplied chart’s missing filter connection, not a newly authored chart that was never connected.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change the supplied dashboard’s date grouping from quarters to months. A revenue card updates to monthly values and comparison text but retains its quarterly title, so the saved heading misdescribes the currently displayed data.
logicalBugs.rootCause: A saved card title is independent of the dashboard temporal-unit parameter. Changing grouping does not rewrite card names, so the seed title becomes misleading when Month is selected. The exact cause remains unresolved. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On the supplied dashboard, change Date Grouping from quarters to months. Its revenue chart updates the displayed period and comparison to months but keeps a quarterly title, so the heading no longer describes the chart’s current data.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open a filter’s selection checklist and reset the applied filter to its default. Results and applied values reset, but the still-open checklist keeps the previous selections instead of showing the values now in effect.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The widget keeps selection in local draft state while dashboard reset updates the applied parameterValues. The open picker does not reinitialize its checked selections for that external reset. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard, open a filter’s checklist of values and then use the filter’s reset-to-default action without closing that checklist. The applied selection and chart results reset, but the open checklist still checks only the previous values and offers Update filter. The draft choices therefore disagree with the restriction now applied to the dashboard.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. The supplied e-commerce example labels a section as customer satisfaction or customer survey responses, but its table contains wine/distillery reviews. This is unrelated seeded content under that advertised section, not a claim that users cannot place arbitrary content on their own dashboards.
logicalBugs.rootCause: This is a seeded query/content mismatch: the survey card selects review bodies whose dataset concerns wine rather than the dashboard products. Rendering source only consumes the stored card query and rows. The exact cause remains unresolved. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: The supplied e-commerce dashboard has a Customer Satisfaction section containing a Customer survey responses table. Its rows are wine and distillery reviews instead of feedback about the dashboard’s products or purchases. This is a mismatch in the supplied example content, not a restriction on what users may put on their own dashboards.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Add a Link card, which is a clickable navigation card, and save the dashboard. Duplicating the whole dashboard omits these Link cards while retaining other cards and tabs; duplicating a tab can preserve them, so the loss is specific to dashboard-copy workflows.
logicalBugs.rootCause: update-cards-for-copy explicitly preserves iframe, text and heading virtual cards but omits link. Link cards have no card_id in id->new-card, so they fall through to the nil/discard branch. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A Link card is a dashboard tile that navigates to another page. Save a dashboard containing external Link cards and duplicate the whole dashboard. The copy retains other cards and tabs but omits those Link cards entirely; duplicating an individual tab can preserve them, so the failure is specific to copying the whole dashboard.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Turn off Auto-apply filters so viewers must click Apply before filter changes run, then duplicate the dashboard. The copy turns Auto-apply back on and immediately executes filter changes instead of retaining the source dashboard’s manual-apply behavior.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The copy endpoint builds dashboard-data from an explicit whitelist of name, description, parameters, creator, collection, position and width; auto_apply_filters is omitted and takes its default. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Turn off Auto-apply filters on a dashboard so changing a filter stages the selection until Apply is clicked, then duplicate that dashboard. The copy has Auto-apply turned on and runs changes immediately instead of preserving the original’s manual-apply behavior. Both full duplication and the dashboard-only copy option exhibit this loss.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Delete the selected tab, restore a revision from before that tab existed, or navigate Back to a removed tab. The remaining tabs still contain cards but none is selected, and the dashboard falsely says there is nothing there until the user manually chooses a surviving tab.
logicalBugs.rootCause: useDashboardUrlQuery router listener parses nextLocation.query.tab and dispatches selectTab for any nonempty changed tab ID without checking that getTabs contains it. Thus a stale browser-history/URL tab can overwrite the reducer's repaired selectedTabId with a deleted ID and hide content. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Dashboard tabs divide a page’s charts and text into separate views. With a later-created tab selected, restore a saved revision from before that tab existed. The surviving tabs still contain content, but none becomes selected and the page says “There’s nothing here, yet” until the user chooses a remaining tab.

On a dashboard with populated tabs, delete the tab that was selected when the page loaded, before clicking any tab manually. No remaining tab is selected, and the page shows its empty-dashboard message instead of the surviving charts. Clicking a tab before performing the deletion avoids this specific setup.

Visit a dashboard tab, delete that tab and save the dashboard, then use browser Back to return to the removed tab’s address. No surviving tab becomes selected and the page appears empty even though other tabs contain charts. It should recover to an existing tab or explain the missing destination.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Give a dashboard filter both a default and “Always require a value”, then open its URL with an explicit empty value for that filter. The empty URL selection bypasses the required default and allows connected queries to run without the intended restriction.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getParameterValueFromQueryParams returns null immediately for maybeParameterValue === empty string, before checking required/default. This URL-clearing branch therefore bypasses the required-value rule. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Give a dashboard filter a default and enable Always require a value, then open the dashboard address with that filter explicitly set to an empty URL value. The required filter becomes blank and its connected chart runs without the intended restriction instead of retaining a value or preventing execution. The same bypass is observed in the public dashboard view.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change a dashboard filter from several values to one, or connect it to a SQL variable that accepts only one value, then save. Previously selected extra values remain applied or sent to the query, producing multi-value results or a card error even when the configuration or visible chip now implies one value.
logicalBugs.rootCause: A dashboard multi-value parameter is forwarded to a single-value native template tag without coercing the applied values to the target tag cardinality. Changing widget configuration also leaves already-applied multiple values intact. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard filter passes selected values into connected chart queries. Start with several selected values, then connect that filter to a saved SQL query’s plain-text input, which accepts only one value. Saving changes the visible control to single-value mode, but the query still receives multiple values and the chart fails; selecting just one value works.

On a dashboard with two values already applied in a filter, edit that filter from Multiple values to A single value and save. The filter still displays two selections and the charts continue aggregating both, instead of reducing the applied selection to match the new single-value configuration.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Set a dashboard date filter to Before or After and choose a specific time as well as a date. Applying it discards the time component, so the connected cards use a date-only boundary rather than the one shown in the picker.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Date parameter normalization/serialization uses the calendar-date operator representation rather than the full datetime endpoint, dropping time before the chart request. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard date filter limits the records used by connected charts. Choose Before or After and enter a specific hour as well as a date. The filter label and address retain that time, but chart results use a date-only boundary, wrongly excluding otherwise matching records later on the selected day. Other date operators and query-editor controls are separate paths.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change a filter default, remove the filter and discard, or save an unrelated filter-label edit after clearing its value. The active selection can adopt the canceled default, lose its prior value, or reinstate a cleared default, and may be remembered on later visits; editing default/configuration state unexpectedly changes the viewer’s applied filter.
logicalBugs.rootCause: setParameterDefaultValue updates the parameter definition and immediately dispatches setParameterValue; edit cancellation restores the definition but not the applied/last-used parameter state. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: In dashboard edit mode, change a filter’s default and then Cancel > Discard changes. The unsaved default nevertheless stays applied to the visible charts and is remembered on later visits. The saved default itself remains unchanged, so discarding configuration edits unexpectedly alters the viewer’s active selection.

Apply a dashboard filter so its connected chart shows only a subset of records. Enter edit mode, remove that filter, then Cancel > Discard changes. The filter control returns but its previous active value does not, leaving it blank and broadening the chart results instead of restoring the pre-edit view.

Clear a dashboard filter that has a saved default, then enter edit mode and change only another filter’s label. Saving the unrelated label edit reapplies the first filter’s default and changes the chart results. The previously cleared selection should remain cleared because the edit did not intentionally change it.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure an existing fixed Between date range, reopen its picker and click the already selected Between mode again. The selected endpoints are rewritten instead of the unchanged mode preserving the range.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Date picker tab selection reconstructs an initial range even when the selected mode is already Between instead of preserving the current endpoints. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Apply a fixed Between date range to a dashboard filter and reopen its picker. Click the already-selected Between tab without choosing a different mode. The endpoint fields change to other dates even though the filter label and calendar highlight retain the original range, instead of an unchanged mode preserving its current endpoints.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A required dashboard filter connected to a SQL variable can still be emptied through its text input. The UI permits the missing-required-value state instead of keeping a value or making its required status enforceable at that control.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The native/text widget forwards an empty edited value without applying the required parameter default/validation used by the clear affordance. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Connect a dashboard filter to a saved SQL query’s text input, give it a default, and enable Always require a value. Its inline input can still be cleared using ordinary typing and submission gestures, leaving the required filter empty instead of preserving or restoring a usable value. This is the direct text-input path, separate from supplying an empty value in the page address.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open the fixed-date Between picker on a phone-width dashboard. Its calendars and controls extend beyond the viewport, leaving part of the range editor unavailable rather than fitting a usable mobile layout.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The date picker renders its two-calendar/fixed-width range content without constraining it to available phone width. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: At phone width, open a dashboard’s date filter and choose Fixed date range > Between. The two-calendar editor is wider than the screen: the end-date field and confirmation control extend beyond the viewport. The offered range picker therefore does not provide a fully visible, usable mobile layout.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Set a numeric Between filter with reversed endpoints and then reopen it. Swapping those values into valid order can leave Update disabled, while the default-value editor can accept a reversed pair without useful validation; distinguish the inability to correct the active filter from an empty result that is mathematically correct for reversed bounds.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getUpdateButtonProps uses areParameterValuesIdentical for current/default/draft comparison. That helper sorts every array before comparing, treating ordered Between endpoints as an unordered selection: [100,50] equals [50,100], disabling a corrective update or labeling a reversed draft Set to default. NumberInputWidget also passes isValid unconditionally, so reversed ranges are not separately rejected. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Apply a numeric Between filter to a dashboard with its lower bound greater than its upper bound, producing the expected empty result. Reopen the picker and swap the endpoints into valid order. Update filter remains disabled, preventing the user from correcting and applying the now-valid range; the defect is correction being blocked, not the original empty result.

Give a dashboard’s numeric Between filter a valid saved default range. Later enter those endpoints in reverse order: the button changes to Set to default, but clicking it applies the reversed values rather than restoring the configured default. The chart then shows no results and reopening retains the inverted range, contradicting the offered reset action.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard text and heading cards render authored Markdown, which can include lists, links and variables whose values come from connected dashboard filters. Set a text card’s horizontal alignment to Center while its content is a Markdown bullet list. The text is centered but bullet markers remain at the left edge, so the list items and their markers do not align together.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Text applies text-align:center to the Markdown container while list-item markers remain outside their content box under standard list styling; marker positioning is not changed with alignment. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard text card is a tile that renders Markdown formatting. Fill it with a bullet list and choose Center horizontal alignment. The item text becomes centered but the bullet markers remain at the card’s left edge instead of aligning beside their items.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard text and heading cards render authored Markdown, which can include lists, links and variables whose values come from connected dashboard filters. Use Middle or Bottom vertical alignment in a text card whose content exceeds its height. Earlier lines overflow above the scroll origin and cannot be reached by ordinary scrolling instead of remaining accessible within the card.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Text applies justify-center/justify-end on a flex-column Markdown container even when its content exceeds available height, positioning overflow before scrollTop=0 and making the top unreachable. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Put more text in a dashboard text card than fits its height, then choose Middle or Bottom vertical alignment. Earlier lines are positioned above the scrollable area and cannot be reached by normal scrolling. The problem is inaccessible overflowed content, rather than text merely starting below the top of the card.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Use Reset to defaults while editing a dashboard card’s visualization. Canceling afterward can retain the reset instead of undoing that draft operation, while a progress-card color changed in the same editor can fail to reset at all; both involve the reset action disagreeing with the editor’s visible settings or commit/cancel boundary.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Visualization reset changes settings through the parent update path rather than keeping an independent complete draft/snapshot, so closing with Cancel cannot restore all previous settings, including progress color. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard table card, save formatting and pagination settings, then reopen its visualization editor and choose Reset to defaults. Cancel that editor, or dismiss it with Escape. The reset remains applied to the card instead of cancellation preserving its previously saved appearance and table behavior.

A dashboard progress card shows a value against a goal using a colored bar. In its visualization editor, change the bar color and then choose Reset to defaults. Both the color swatch and preview remain on the changed color instead of restoring the default, so the reset does not undo that draft setting.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Configure a card’s custom click destination, then change an unrelated visualization setting and save. Clicking the card reverts to the standard drill menu instead of its saved custom action; changing appearance unexpectedly replaces navigation behavior.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashcard visualization settings save replaces the settings object without preserving the separate click_behavior entry, falling back to default drill-through. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Configure a dashboard chart so clicking it performs a custom action, such as updating a connected filter. Change an unrelated visualization option or title and save. Clicking the chart now opens its ordinary drill-through menu instead of the previously configured action, so editing appearance discards navigation/filter behavior.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change the dashboard’s title to spaces only. Inline editing leaves a blank header until reload even though the save was rejected; the full edit form instead reports “Save failed” without explaining the invalid name. An exactly empty title that correctly restores the prior name is not the same failure.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashboard title editing/submission checks raw nonempty input instead of trimmed content; the API rejects the nonblank name contract but the inline/editor state is not restored or explained. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Rename a dashboard inline to spaces only and finish the edit by clicking away or pressing Enter. The title remains visibly blank without an error, even though the server rejected the rename and reloading restores the previous saved title. This is a misleading unsaved header, not a successfully stored blank name.

In the full dashboard editor, replace the title with spaces only and click Save. The editor stays open and briefly says Save failed, but gives no explanation that the title is invalid. The missing validation feedback leaves the user unable to identify why this particular save was rejected.

logicalBugs.description: Global search finds saved questions, dashboards, models and metrics, and can restrict results by content type, date or whether an item is in Trash. Permanently delete a dashboard, then search with “Search items in trash” enabled. The deleted dashboard still appears as a result whose link opens a not-found page, rather than disappearing from search once it no longer exists.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Search result indexing/invalidation outlives the deleted dashboard entity; clicking the stale hit requests a removed dashboard and produces Not found. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard is a saved page of charts and text that may first be moved to Trash. Permanently delete one, then use global search with Search items in trash enabled. The dashboard still appears, but its result opens Page Not Found instead of disappearing once the underlying item is permanently gone.

logicalBugs.description: Questions are saved queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved aggregate calculations. Each has a title, a collection location and revision history. Opening History on a dashboard, model or metric can show “undefined modified this” where the person’s name should be. The observable failure is the literal missing-name text in an existing revision entry, not the absence of history or a claim that an unauthorized actor edited the item.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Timeline revision copy reads r.user.common_name directly for another actor, without reconstructing a name or providing a fallback when the seeded revision user lacks that property. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Open More info > History on an existing dashboard. A saved revision entry reads “undefined modified this” where the editing person’s name should appear. This concerns the literal missing-name text in an available history entry, not missing revisions or evidence of an unauthorized edit.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure a filter embedded inside a card with a default and “Always require a value”, then duplicate that card. The copied local filter loses its default or required-value choice instead of carrying those settings with the copied card.
logicalBugs.rootCause: duplicateParameters passes _.omit(parameter,"id") into createParameter, but createParameter constructs a fresh object containing only id, name, slug, type and sectionId. Default, required, widget/source configuration and other inline options are discarded. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard card can have its own embedded filter rather than using a page-wide control. Give that local numeric filter a default range and enable Always require a value, then duplicate the card. The copy loses the default and required setting and can show rows outside the source range instead of preserving the local filter configuration.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Create a tab containing filters embedded in text/heading cards and connected question cards, then duplicate the tab. Copied text can show raw variable syntax, opening a copied filter can jump to the original tab, or copied questions can ignore the displayed selection and show unfiltered totals; the copied controls and their card connections no longer describe the same tab.
logicalBugs.rootCause: duplicateTab copies sourceDashCard by spread and replaces only id/dashboard_tab_id/isDirty. It does not clone dashboard parameters or rewrite inline parameter ownership and text mappings to the new card/tab. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Create a dashboard tab with a heading and text tile whose variable placeholders both display the value from a filter embedded in the heading. Duplicate the tab and save. The copied heading still shows the chosen value, but the copied text tile displays its raw placeholder even after reload, instead of retaining the same connection.

Duplicate a dashboard tab containing a heading with its own embedded text filter, then save and re-enter edit mode on the copied tab. Clicking the copied heading’s filter jumps selection and the address back to the original tab and opens its settings there. The user cannot configure the copied control in place.

Connect a filter embedded in a dashboard heading to both that heading’s text variable and a chart’s product-category field, then duplicate the tab. On the copy, the heading and filter still name the chosen category, but the chart shows totals across all categories and ignores further selection changes. The copied chart lost a connection that the copied controls still advertise.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A member opens More info for a dashboard created by another authorized user. “Creator and last editor” omits the creator row even though the dashboard has a valid creator, rather than displaying that person’s identity.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DashboardDetails fetches the creator with useGetUserQuery(dashboard.creator_id) and renders the entire creator row only when creator exists. A member denied that user-detail endpoint sees no creator fallback even though the dashboard itself is readable. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: As a member who can view a dashboard created by another user, open More info and inspect Creator and last editor. The last editor appears but the creator row is missing even though History identifies a valid creator. The failure is the omitted creator information, not absence of all dashboard metadata.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open the editor for an existing internal Metabase link card and save it without intentionally changing its target. The stored destination becomes malformed or points to the wrong location, so merely editing the card damages a link that previously worked.
logicalBugs.rootCause: LinkViz editor parses a saved internal URL into entity/link state and serializes it back with a different destination representation, even when the user makes no change. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Save a dashboard Link card targeting another Metabase page, then open its pencil editor and save without changing the target. The link becomes malformed or points to the wrong place instead of preserving the previously working internal destination. Merely revisiting and confirming the editor damages the saved link.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Apply a numeric Between filter with its lower endpoint empty and only an upper endpoint entered. After reload, that upper value moves into the lower field and reverses the predicate from “at most” to “at least”; the lower field may have been left empty intentionally or cleared by invalid text.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The approximate public source deserializeNumberParameterValue explicitly preserves a two-item [null,upper] array for number/between. Endpoint position must therefore be lost earlier in URL/value transport or the actual runtime implementation; this parser alone does not establish the root. The exact cause remains unresolved. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Apply a dashboard’s numeric Between filter with only an upper bound, leaving the lower field intentionally empty. Reload the dashboard. The upper value moves into the lower field and results change from “at most this value” to “at least this value,” rather than preserving the accepted one-sided range.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open an empty dashboard while it is in Trash. It still offers Add a chart, leading users into an edit that fails with a permission error when saved instead of hiding or explaining the unavailable action.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The empty dashboard state chooses its creation action from edit capability without also checking archived state, allowing an invalid edit/save flow on a trashed dashboard. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Move an empty dashboard to Trash and open it there. It still offers Add a chart and permits entering the editor, but adding a chart and saving ends on a permission-denied page. Reload confirms nothing was saved, so the interface offers an edit flow that cannot finish while the dashboard remains trashed.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure a custom filter choice whose displayed label maps to an empty stored value, then select it and refresh. The selected custom label disappears or resets instead of surviving as the configured empty-value choice.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Parameter URL parsing treats an empty raw string as null/cleared, so a selected display label whose actual value is empty cannot round-trip as a selection. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Configure a dashboard filter’s custom list with a visible label whose underlying value is empty. Select that label alongside other choices and apply it; the selection count includes it. After refresh, the empty-valued choice disappears and the count drops instead of preserving or rejecting that configured choice explicitly.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Edit only the dashboard title or description, or trash it, and inspect History. It can also claim a pin-position, card or tab modification that the user did not make, especially on the first edit after reverting a revision; this is misleading change narration rather than the cards actually being edited in that operation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashboard revision serialization/restoration retains normalized positional/card/tab metadata; subsequent rename/edit diff compares different snapshots and reports those non-user edits as changes. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Duplicate a dashboard in a collection containing pinned dashboard shortcuts, so the operation changes the surrounding pin positions. On the copy, change only its title and inspect History. The entry also claims a pin-position change, although the rename itself did not change its position.

On a dashboard, remove a chart or tab and save, then use History to restore the revision that brings it back. Make a subsequent title-only, description-only or trash change. The first history entry after restoration also claims that cards or tabs were modified even though their visible arrangement stayed unchanged.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure a chart link that opens the same dashboard with another filter value, follow it, then use browser Back. The clicked destination’s category remains applied instead of restoring the filter state from before following the link.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashboard parameter synchronization updates the current URL/history state while following a link to the same dashboard, overwriting or reapplying the clicked category instead of retaining a distinct prior parameter snapshot. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Configure clicking a dashboard chart to open another tab of the same dashboard with a narrower filter selection. Follow that link and use browser Back to return to the source. The destination’s category remains applied instead of restoring the source’s earlier selection; the first Back can also leave the destination tab visible.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Save a custom URL destination on a gauge card, then click the displayed value or gauge arc. Neither opens the destination, although the chart exposes settings for that click behavior.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Gauge forwards onVisualizationClick to segment labels; its main scalar value and arc do not produce the click object required for a custom destination. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A gauge card displays a value on a dial inside a dashboard. Save a custom URL click destination for that card, then click its central value or arc. Neither navigates or offers a link prompt, despite the card’s accepted click configuration.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Use a funnel chart’s Bar display and save a custom dashboard click destination. Clicking the rendered bars does not invoke that destination, even though it is configured for the card.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The funnel bar renderer transforms rows for the display without preserving/dispatching the dashboard click context needed for saved custom click behavior. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Place a funnel chart on a dashboard and set its funnel display to Bar chart, then save a custom click destination pointing to another dashboard. Clicking its rendered bars shows only a data tooltip or leaves the same page visible. It does not open the configured destination or pass the mapped filter value.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Edit the Goal number of a progress chart by typing a longer value with a decimal. Intermediate updates remove or reorder digits, leaving a different goal and preview instead of the entered number; the problem occurs during normal typing, not only after a saved reload.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Progress Goal is controlled through numeric parsing and immediate visualization setting feedback; incomplete decimal/input states are reformatted and sent back to the active input rather than retained as text until commit. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard progress card compares a value with its configured Goal. In its visualization editor, select the current Goal and type a longer number containing a decimal using normal keystrokes. Digits disappear or reorder during editing, leaving a different goal and a contradictory preview before anything is saved.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Create a conditional-formatting rule for an ID column whose displayed values are remapped to related names. The rule saves but does not tint the matching table row, even though its underlying ID meets the condition.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Conditional formatting compares the displayed/remapped value against the raw-field rule without consistently resolving the remapped column/value pair. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Add a table card whose numeric ID column is displayed using related human-readable names. Save a conditional-formatting rule that should color an entire row when that ID equals a known matching value. The rule remains saved, but the matching row stays uncolored in both preview and the dashboard instead of receiving the chosen tint.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Open visualization settings for an existing funnel chart without changing any setting. Its stage ordering and comparison baseline immediately change in the preview instead of preserving the saved funnel’s order.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Funnel settings/default normalization recomputes row sorting and first-stage baseline when the editor preview is initialized rather than preserving the saved display settings unchanged. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Open a saved funnel chart’s visualization editor without changing any setting. The funnel’s stages immediately reorder alphabetically and its percentage baseline changes, so values can exceed 100% against a different first stage. Simply opening settings should preserve the saved stage order and baseline.

logicalBugs.description: Global search finds saved questions, dashboards, models and metrics, and can restrict results by content type, date or whether an item is in Trash. Use Creation date’s “Before” search filter with a selected calendar date. Results still include items created on that very day, rather than only earlier days; this is the exclusive-boundary error even when the item’s displayed timezone/day is otherwise consistent.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The absolute ~date decoder returns the selected date as :end. Search requests date-string->range with inclusive-end? false, whose adjust-inclusive-range-if-needed adds one day to the end; search then compares timestamp-date < that advanced bound. This makes Before include the selected day. The conversion must distinguish an already-exclusive Before endpoint from an inclusive range endpoint. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Create a dashboard and verify its creation date, then search for it using the Creation date filter’s Before operator with that same date. It remains in the results, just as it does under On that date, instead of being excluded by an exclusive “before” boundary. This is separate from a timezone disagreement about which day it was created.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Map clicking a timestamp result column to a dashboard Date Range filter. Clicking a value sets an invalid range and makes connected charts fail instead of filtering them to the selected timestamp’s supported date interval.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashboard click parameter mapping serializes a timestamp/datetime cell directly into a date-range parameter instead of using that parameter operator and expected range encoding. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: In a dashboard table card, configure clicks on a timestamp column to update the page’s Date Range filter. Click a date value and inspect charts connected to that filter, including on another tab. The filter becomes blank and the charts fail to load instead of applying a valid date derived from the clicked value.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Move a card to another dashboard tab, then invoke Undo while on the destination tab. The resulting tab/card state cannot be saved, although the undo action should leave a valid dashboard arrangement.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Move/undo restores a dashcard tab assignment from stale destination/source state, but the tab normalization/save payload no longer recognizes the restored assignment. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard with several tabs, move a text card to another tab and select that destination tab. Click Undo in the move notification, then save without returning to the original tab. Save fails and leaves the editor open instead of accepting the restored arrangement that Undo produced.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Scroll the dashboard tab bar to its last tabs, then enter edit mode. The final tab becomes clipped but the right-scroll arrow is absent, so the newly reduced visible space cannot be navigated normally.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DashboardTabs scroll/overflow state is measured before edit controls change available width and is not recalculated for that transition. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Add enough dashboard tabs to overflow their horizontal strip, scroll fully right to expose the last tab, then enter edit mode. Extra edit controls reduce the available width and clip that final tab and its menu, but no right-scroll arrow appears to reach them. The newly hidden controls are therefore inaccessible through the normal tab navigation.

logicalBugs.description: Column and chart formatting control how numbers are displayed, including decimal places, currency labels and custom prefixes; these controls should represent the saved display settings. Enter an excessive number of decimal places, such as 101, in a column or chart’s formatting settings. It is accepted without validation, but previews or saved charts then show incorrect integers, all-zero percentage labels or a rendering error instead of a correctly formatted number.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared decimals setting has only nonnegative/integer checks and no formatter maximum. Values above the supported precision range reach scalar/gauge/pie number formatters, producing warnings or fallback integer/zero labels. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard card displaying a single number, enter an unsupported very large decimal-place count, such as 101, in formatting settings and save. The preview and saved card show a persistent warning icon instead of the number, including after reload. The invalid setting is accepted without the validation needed to keep the card renderable.

On a dashboard gauge card displaying a fractional value, set decimal places to an unsupported large value such as 101. The field accepts it without feedback, but the gauge displays a whole integer and retains that display after saving and reload. It neither honors the requested precision nor explains or rejects it.

On a dashboard pie or donut chart, replace a valid decimal-place setting with an unsupported large value such as 101. Nonzero slice and legend percentages all become zero while the chart still has substantial slices and an unchanged total. Saving and reload preserve these incorrect labels instead of validating the precision.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Edit a combination chart, which displays several series or chart types together, using Average for a series. Its preview shows one monthly aggregate, but saving produces a different value for that same month instead of matching the previewed aggregation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashboard chart editor preview and saved multiseries transform use different series/column mapping settings, so the same displayed Average is regrouped/re-aggregated after save. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: In a dashboard chart editor, start from a funnel-aggregated monthly series, switch to a combination chart and add an Average metric alongside the existing sum. The preview shows one monthly average, but saving and reloading halves the displayed average for the same month without changing the metric label. The saved chart and reopened editor therefore disagree with the value previewed before saving.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Start creating a new dashboard while viewing a missing-dashboard or permission-denied error route. The new dashboard is created, but the old error screen remains instead of opening the new dashboard.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Dashboard creation navigation reuses DashboardApp state that still contains the previous missing/denied dashboard error rather than resetting it for the newly created dashboard. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: While viewing a missing-dashboard or permission-denied error page, choose New > Dashboard and complete creation. The new dashboard is saved and can be found and opened manually, but the creation dialog closes onto the old error route instead of opening the new dashboard’s editor.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. With a dashboard tab selected, open Duplicate or Move and then cancel the dialog. The tab query parameter is removed from the address even though the selected dashboard view was not intentionally changed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The routed Duplicate/Move modal close location is constructed from the dashboard pathname without retaining its tab query, replacing the selected-tab URL on cancellation. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Select a nondefault dashboard tab, open the Duplicate or Move dialog and cancel or close it without completing the action. The current tab remains visible, but the address loses its tab and filter parameters. Reopening or reloading that address resets to the default tab instead of preserving the view that was never intentionally changed.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. While editing a dashboard, use browser Back and cancel the warning about leaving unsaved changes. The editor stays visible but the address remains the attempted collection destination instead of being restored to the dashboard being edited.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Route cancellation retains the dashboard editor but fails to restore the browser/router URL from the already attempted collection transition, leaving view state and address inconsistent. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Open a dashboard from its collection, enter edit mode and make an unsaved change. Press browser Back, then Cancel the discard-changes warning. The dashboard editor and draft stay visible, but the address still points to the attempted collection destination instead of returning to the dashboard address.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure clicking a chart column to update a dashboard filter, then delete that filter and save. The click-behavior editor still lists the removed target, while clicking neither applies a filter nor opens the normal drill menu, leaving an action that cannot do what its configuration claims.
logicalBugs.rootCause: removeParameter removes dashboard/card parameter mappings but does not remove references to that parameter in visualization_settings.click_behavior, so clicks target a nonexistent filter. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Configure a dashboard table column’s click action to update a page filter, verify it works, then delete that filter and save. The click-settings editor still claims the column updates a filter, but clicks neither filter the table nor open the ordinary drill-through menu. The deleted target remains configured as if it were usable.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. In Duplicate dashboard, delete the source description so the copy should have none. The new dashboard instead restores the original description, rather than honoring the cleared field.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The copy endpoint uses (or description (:description existing-dashboard)); the cleared form normalizes to nil, which is treated as an absent override and replaced with source description. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Open Duplicate for a dashboard that has a description, clear the optional Description field in the copy dialog and finish creating the copy. The new dashboard’s More info panel shows the source description after refresh instead of honoring the explicit blank value.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Rename a dashboard filter using only spaces and save. The control persists with a blank-looking label rather than rejecting the unusable name or restoring its previous label.
logicalBugs.rootCause: parameters/utils/dashboards.setParameterName spreads the parameter and assigns name:name plus slugify(name) without trimming or rejecting blank-after-trim names. Whitespace labels persist while their slug can be empty. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard filter has a label so viewers can identify what records it restricts. Rename that label to spaces only and save. The blank-looking label persists after reload, leaving an icon and dropdown without a readable name instead of rejecting or restoring the unusable label.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. In dashboard editing, open an unselected populated tab’s menu and choose Duplicate. The menu stays open and no new tab, dialog or explanation appears; the user need not know whether that tab’s question results have already been fetched.
logicalBugs.rootCause: duplicateTab indexes state.dashcardData[sourceDashCard.id][sourceDashCard.card_id] without optional chaining; a tab with a nonvirtual card whose data was not loaded causes the reducer to throw instead of duplicating. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: In dashboard edit mode, open the menu of a populated tab that is not currently selected and choose Duplicate. The menu stays open and no tab, workflow or error appears. The offered duplication action does not proceed even though the tab contains charts that can be opened normally.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Enable a trend line on a chart with plotted data. The line lies substantially away from the series rather than fitting the visible values, so its position misrepresents the trend rather than just using a different label or color.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Regression fitting and chart-axis/date transformation do not use the same x coordinate origin/scale, so the computed line is displaced from the plotted time series. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Enable a trend line on a dashboard chart with plotted numeric series. The fitted dotted line remains near the baseline rather than running through the visible rising values; isolating the series does not repair it. Its position therefore misrepresents the numeric trend, rather than merely differing in label or color.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open a filter attached to one dashboard card and click an available value’s checkbox. The selection does not change and Update remains disabled, preventing the chosen value from being applied even though the option is visibly available.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Inline parameter dropdown selection is intercepted by the surrounding dashcard/edit interaction layer before the widget selection update takes effect. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Open a value-selection filter embedded in one dashboard card, then click an available option’s checkbox. The checkbox does not change and Update filter remains disabled, preventing the option from being applied. This concerns the offered card-local checkbox interaction, not a missing filter value.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. A nested pie chart has inner parent groups and outer child categories. Clicking an inner parent segment applies the first child’s category filter instead of the selected parent group, so navigation restricts to a different level of the chart.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The pie click event maps the aggregate parent node to one representative leaf row, losing the full parent grouping context and producing the first child category filter. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard’s nested pie chart shows parent periods in its inner ring and child categories outside them. Click an inner parent segment configured to update filters. The date range updates, but the first child category is also arbitrarily selected, narrowing the results to one child instead of the chosen parent aggregate.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Enable a logarithmic value axis on a horizontal Row chart while retaining the default manual minimum of zero. The chart disappears without identifying that incompatible zero boundary or giving a usable validation message.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The chart settings accept manual minimum zero while log scale is selected and do not validate the logarithmic domain before rendering, leaving an empty chart. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard’s horizontal Row chart, choose a logarithmic value scale while the default manual axis minimum remains zero. The bars and numeric ticks disappear, leaving labels and axis lines without an explanation that zero is incompatible with the scale. The offered change should remain usable or identify the boundary needing correction.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A relative-date “Starting from” offset specifies how far before or after the present an interval begins. Entering a fractional offset can blank the applied label and break connected chart queries, while changing an existing valid offset to zero can leave the old filter applied despite the preview updating; these are offset-entry failures, not consistent whole-number normalization.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared relative-date numeric controls/parser assume positive integers but do not validate/canonicalize typed fractions and zero consistently with preview/query serialization. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Apply a dashboard relative-date filter, then reopen it and change its Starting from offset to a fractional number. Applying the edit blanks the filter label and makes connected charts show an error; reopening no longer displays the configured relative editor. The unsupported value is accepted without feedback instead of keeping the filter and charts recoverable.

Start with an applied dashboard relative-date range that has a nonzero Starting from offset. Reopen it, choose a new interval and set that offset to zero, then click Update filter. The preview changes, but the dialog stays open and the old filter and chart dates remain applied without explaining why the new range cannot be submitted.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Add another question as a series to a dashboard card and enable “Hide this card if there are no results”. If the primary question is empty, the entire card hides even when the added series has visible data, instead of considering the combined result.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The approximate public source shouldHideCard already calls hasRows(dashcardData), which scans all query results, rather than checking just the main card. The report therefore requires tracing which series were present in the runtime dashcardData map or examining the actual build; a blanket main-card-only predicate is contradicted by this source. The exact cause remains unresolved. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard card can plot a primary saved query together with additional query series. Add a series that has data, then enable Hide this card if there are no results while the primary query is empty. The entire card disappears despite the added series having visible results, instead of considering all the plotted data.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change an existing dashboard filter’s type or comparison, such as Quarter to Date Range or Between to Greater than or equal to, and save a new default. The old incompatible applied selection returns instead, so the chip and picker disagree and connected charts can fail even though the new configuration was saved.
logicalBugs.rootCause: setParameterType resets mappings and changes the parameter definition via setParamType/restoreValueConfigIfNeeded, but never dispatches a corresponding conversion/reset of the existing parameterValues. A prior Quarter/range value can therefore remain applied under a new parameter type/operator. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard, apply a Quarter and Year filter value and let the page remember it. Change that filter to Date Range, choose a new default interval and save. After refresh the old quarter selection returns, while reopening shows different date-picker values, so the applied restriction no longer matches the saved type/default.

On a dashboard chart, apply a numeric Between filter with two endpoints. Edit it to Greater than or equal to, set a new single-number default and save. The old pair returns as “2 selections” and the chart errors instead of applying a value compatible with the new comparison.

logicalBugs.description: Global search finds saved questions, dashboards, models and metrics, and can restrict results by content type, date or whether an item is in Trash. Search by Creation date or Last edit using Today or a fixed calendar day and compare the results with the item’s displayed dates. Recently created or edited items can be excluded from Today, and fixed-date and relative-date choices can disagree; reported scope includes models, metrics, questions and seeded items never edited since creation. A browser/server midnight boundary is one observed trigger, not evidence that every matching report must establish a timezone diagnosis.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Search date-range-filter-clause calls date-string->range without a viewer timezone. Relative decoding obtains t/local-date-time on the server, while the search comparison casts stored timestamps to date; browser-local date picks and previews therefore need not describe the same day near a timezone boundary. Exact fixture timezone configuration remains a prerequisite of each report. Seeded or never-edited item variants are now accepted by the source matching scope; the supplied evidence does not establish that each such exclusion has the same timezone cause rather than missing last-edit metadata. Attribution of those broader symptoms remains provisional. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Use global search to find dashboards by name and confirm that a fixed Creation date matches their displayed creation day. Change to a relative-date filter whose preview advertises that same day. Applying it can show a different label such as Tomorrow and omit those dashboards instead of matching the fixed-date results. This path concerns dashboard search and disagreement between the picker’s preview and applied calendar day.

logicalBugs.description: A Metabase dashboard is a page of chart or table cards, and each filter must be connected to the cards it should affect. Duplicating a filtered card can lose that connection and show unfiltered values while the original remains filtered. Copying an entire dashboard can instead leave a filter inside a card claiming The selected filter is on another tab, even though the filter and its card are visible on the same copied tab, preventing access to its field connection settings.
logicalBugs.rootCause: duplicateCard changes dashcard ID and duplicates inline parameter IDs, but not every associated parameter/card ownership reference is remapped consistently, causing a lost dashboard filter connection or an own-card parameter classified as another tab. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard, connect a page-wide category filter to a revenue card and apply one category so the chart shows a restricted total. Duplicate the card using its own toolbar. The new card shows the all-category total while the original stays filtered, instead of copying the source card’s filter connection.

Configure a filter inside a dashboard table card, then duplicate the whole dashboard using Only duplicate the dashboard. On the copy, edit the local filter visible on that same table and selected tab. Instead of its field-mapping controls, the card says “The selected filter is on another tab,” preventing inspection of a connection that should belong to this copied card.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A member edits unrelated text on a dashboard that contains a link to a private dashboard they cannot access. Saving damages that link’s retained destination information, so even its owner later sees permission denied where the link previously worked.
logicalBugs.rootCause: A reader without access sees redacted link entity metadata; dashboard save serializes that redacted representation over the stored link, so the original private destination becomes inaccessible even to its owner. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard contains a Link card targeting another user’s private dashboard. A member without access to that destination edits only unrelated text and saves the containing dashboard. The link then shows permission denied even to its authorized owner, although the destination still opens directly, so the unrelated save damages the link rather than changing destination permissions.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Combine multiple question series in a chart and map clicking its category to a filter on a destination dashboard. The editor accepts the mapping, but clicking clears that category filter instead of passing the selected series value.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ClickMappings resolves the destination parameter against untransformed source column names, while combined-series chart clicks expose remapped column IDs, leaving the mapped value undefined and clearing the filter. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Combine several saved-query series in one dashboard chart, then configure clicks to open another dashboard and pass the clicked category into its filter. The editor accepts that mapping, but clicking a series value clears the destination category filter instead of passing the selected value, even while another mapped date filter updates.

logicalBugs.description: An X-ray is an automatically generated collection of charts intended to explain a selected field, record group or query result. Choose Automatic insights → X-ray from a dashboard chart showing an aggregated revenue/order period. The destination is an empty analysis dashboard rather than generated insights for the selected aggregate and its grouping context.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Automatic insights builds X-ray query context from the clicked aggregation without retaining all temporal grouping and parameter constraints, yielding an empty analysis query. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Metabase’s X-ray action generates explanatory charts for selected data. Choose Automatic insights > X-ray from a populated dashboard chart showing an aggregated revenue/order period. The destination says the dashboard is empty instead of producing insights for that aggregate or explaining why they are unavailable.

logicalBugs.description: An X-ray is an automatically generated collection of charts intended to explain a selected field, record group or query result. Open an automatically generated X-ray for a selected geographic state. The page says it is analyzing that state, but some revenue charts include rows from other states instead of retaining the advertised State restriction.
logicalBugs.rootCause: X-ray card generation does not consistently propagate the source State=SD filter to every generated revenue query, while the dashboard description still reflects the selected state. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Open an automatically generated X-ray, a page of explanatory charts, for a selected geographic state. Its heading says it analyzes that state, but some revenue charts include values from other states. The chart results therefore violate the page’s advertised state restriction instead of explaining only the selected subset.

logicalBugs.description: An X-ray is an automatically generated collection of charts intended to explain a selected field, record group or query result. Choose “Zoom in: State” on a state-level revenue map.
