The destination map has no usable matching geography columns and displays configuration guidance rather than a working view of the selected state.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The map zoom drill generates a new map query/display without ensuring the breakout provides the geospatial columns required by the target map mode. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a state-level revenue map in an automatically generated analysis, choose Zoom in: State. The destination shows a placeholder map and instructions to configure geography columns instead of a usable map of the selected state. The offered navigation leads to an unconfigured visualization rather than the promised geographic detail.

logicalBugs.description: A Metabase single-number chart can display a currency amount with a written currency name, such as euros, and can abbreviate large amounts with Compact number formatting. After selecting the Name currency label and enabling Compact number formatting, the preview uses a currency symbol instead of the written name even though the selector still says Name. The chosen label style and the rendered value disagree; the selection itself remains visible.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Scalar number formatting applies compact defaults by rewriting currency_style to symbol, overriding the independently selected Name setting. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard’s single-number chart, select the currency Name label and then enable Compact number formatting. The selector still says Name, but the preview replaces the written currency name with a symbol instead of only abbreviating the amount. The mismatch is between the chosen style and rendered value, not a missing saved selection.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard text and heading cards render authored Markdown, which can include lists, links and variables whose values come from connected dashboard filters. Place a filter variable inside a Markdown link in a text card, then apply a value containing spaces. The rendered card shows raw link syntax rather than a clickable link because the substituted URL is not kept valid.
logicalBugs.rootCause: fillParametersInText supports urlEncode but defaults it to false. Text calls it with escapeMarkdown:true and never enables urlEncode, so spaces in substituted filter values remain literal spaces in Markdown destinations and invalidate the link syntax. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard text tile can render a Markdown link containing a variable connected to a filter. Start with a working link, then apply a variable value containing spaces or URL-special characters. The tile displays the raw Markdown link syntax instead of a clickable link, so inserting the selected value breaks an otherwise valid destination.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Visit multiple dashboard tabs, use browser Back, and change a filter on the restored tab. Browser Forward no longer restores the subsequently visited tab and its filter selection, even though changing that filter should not destroy the existing forward destination.
logicalBugs.rootCause: useDashboardUrlQuery listens to browser navigation and dispatches selectTab when the URL tab changes. A separate effect treats the resulting queryParams.tab change as a new user tab change and dispatches push, creating a new entry after Back and clearing the previous Forward history. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Visit several tabs of a dashboard and choose filter values, then use browser Back and change a filter on the restored tab. Browser Forward no longer restores the tab and selection visited after that history entry. A local filter change unexpectedly replaces the existing forward destination.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. While editing a filter, choose an input style such as Search box and then change its comparison operator. The style immediately returns to the previously saved choice, such as Input box, discarding the unsaved style edit before the configuration is submitted.
logicalBugs.rootCause: restoreParameterMappingsIfNeeded replaces the edited parameter with parameterToRestore from dashboardBeforeEditing via setParamType. That full prior object includes the old widget settings, overwriting a widget-style change made earlier in the current unsaved edit. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: While editing a dashboard filter, choose an unsaved input style such as Search box and then change its comparison operator. The style immediately reverts to the previously saved Input box choice instead of preserving the pending style edit until submission. This loss happens inside configuration before the dashboard is saved.

logicalBugs.description: A query filter restricts which rows are returned; its editor selects a column, a comparison and the values to compare. Enter a literal %, underscore or backslash in a text Contains, Does not contain, Starts with or Ends with filter. These characters are treated as pattern instructions instead of ordinary text, so rows can match without containing the entered character or be wrongly excluded; the same defect appears in graphical filters and SQL field-filter controls.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SQL starts-with/contains/ends-with generate LIKE patterns by concatenating user values with wildcards without escaping literal %/_ or backslashes. This shared compiler serves notebook text filters and SQL field-filter operators, so literal-percent matching becomes wildcard matching. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Add a dashboard text filter using Starts with and connect it to a category column whose values do not begin with a percent sign. Apply a literal % as the filter value. The chart still displays all categories after refresh instead of no matches, treating the character as a wildcard rather than the text the user entered.

logicalBugs.description: A Metabase scatter chart displays individual data points and can be configured to open a particular address when a point is clicked. After saving that custom destination, clicking a plotted point opens the normal drill-through menu, with actions such as Filter by this value or View details, instead of navigating to the chosen address. The failure is ignoring the saved click destination on those points; the click itself is recognized.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The scatter renderer/settings permit saved click behavior but the point event path does not produce or dispatch the custom destination click context consistently. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard scatter chart, save a custom URL click destination for its numeric data column. Reload and click a plotted point. The default drill-through menu opens and the custom destination is not followed, even though reopening click settings confirms the saved URL; this is a wrong click action rather than a click with no visible response.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change both a custom link’s text and destination, then close the URL dialog with its X without completing it. The edited text remains but the edited URL is discarded, leaving only part of that canceled link edit applied.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CustomURLPicker keeps url in local state until Done/handleSubmit, but passes updateSettings directly to CustomLinkText. Link text is therefore committed immediately while the URL remains an uncommitted local draft. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: In a dashboard table column’s custom-link editor, change both the displayed link text and URL, then close the URL dialog with X instead of Done. The old URL remains, but the new link text is applied and can persist after dashboard Save. Closing the dialog therefore discards only part of the same unconfirmed link edit.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A dashboard remembers the viewer’s previous filter choices, but opening it through a URL that only specifies a tab discards and overwrites those remembered choices. Selecting a tab unexpectedly resets independent filters even when the URL supplies no replacement values for them.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getParameterValueFromQueryParams uses Object.keys(params).length > 0 to decide whether URL parameters exist. A tab query alone makes hasQueryParams true, so every absent filter falls back to its default instead of lastUsedValues. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: A dashboard remembers the viewer’s previously used filter values. Open it through an address specifying only which tab to display, without giving replacement filter values. The remembered filters are cleared and that cleared state is saved for later visits, even though selecting a tab should not reset independent record restrictions.

logicalBugs.description: A date/time filter selects rows by a calendar date or an interval; the picker’s displayed dates and preview should describe the timestamps actually included. Type a fractional interval such as 0.5 into a relative-date picker and leave the field. The input can show 1 while its preview and applied filter use 5 units, so two simultaneously displayed controls disagree; this is different from an unsupported fraction that is visibly normalized consistently before applying.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DateIntervalPicker uses NumberInputWithFallbackValue with decimal entry disabled. The component keeps a display string separately from the parent interval; transient fractional text followed by fallback-on-blur can leave displayed and applied numbers inconsistent. The precise fixture transaction ordering is inferred, rather than runtime-verified. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: In a dashboard relative-date filter, type a fractional interval and leave the field. The numeric input normalizes to one unit while the preview and applied range still use a different multi-unit interval. This is contradictory simultaneous state, separately from an unsupported fraction consistently normalized everywhere before applying.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open a dashboard with filter values in its address, make an edit and save. The reload drops those URL values and restores older remembered selections instead, so text/heading cards can lose their filter and other cards can show earlier results despite the active selection before saving.
logicalBugs.rootCause: After saving, updateDashboard calls fetchDashboard with queryParams:null and options.preserveParameters:false to clear editing state. This deliberately discards current parameter state and reinitializes from default/last-used values; the source comment documents a related race on slow networks. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Open a dashboard with active filter values in its address, including filters supplying variables in heading/text tiles. Make an unrelated dashboard content edit and save. The reload clears those selections or restores older remembered values, so previously substituted text and filtered charts no longer reflect the selection active before saving.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Move a dashboard to another collection and inspect its More info details immediately afterward. Its last-editor information still identifies the earlier edit until refresh instead of reflecting the completed move.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The move mutation updates collection_id while the mounted dashboard info retains the old last_edit_info object; its cache is not refreshed from the server until reload. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Move a dashboard to another collection, then immediately open More info. The Saved in location updates, but the last-editor row still names the previous editor until refresh. The completed move’s metadata is therefore shown inconsistently in the same information panel.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Apply numeric filter choices with custom displayed labels, then refresh the dashboard. The labels disappear and the picker can list duplicate choices for the same numbers, even though the underlying selections were saved.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Parameter URL/selection parsing coerces numeric raw values while custom-list options retain another raw value type; strict option matching fails, creating raw-value duplicates without the saved labels. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: Give numeric choices in a dashboard filter custom display labels, apply them and refresh. Selected choices return as raw numbers while separate unchecked choices still show the configured labels. The charts remain filtered, but one logical value appears twice and its selected label is lost instead of round-tripping correctly.

logicalBugs.description: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. While a dashboard already has unsaved edits, press its “e” edit shortcut. It exits editing and drops the draft without a discard warning instead of preserving the active edit session.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The dashboard keyboard shortcut toggles edit state regardless of isEditing/dirty state, invoking the cancel/discard path without a confirmation. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard with unsaved editing changes, press its e shortcut while already in edit mode. The editor closes and the pending cards disappear without the discard confirmation offered by Cancel. Entering edit mode again shows the unchanged saved dashboard, confirming the draft was dropped rather than saved.

logicalBugs.description: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Apply a filter to a dashboard chart using a time-period comparison. Its comparison label displays a number followed by the literal word “undefined” instead of the intended time unit.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Comparison period label generation indexes an unavailable temporal unit/period descriptor after filtered series normalization, interpolating undefined rather than a valid unit label. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution. This analysis uses approximate public source because the fixture’s exact runtime source revision was unavailable.
reproductionPaths: On a dashboard number chart with a saved period comparison, apply a dashboard filter and inspect the comparison label. A label such as “4 quarters ago” becomes “4 undefined” instead of retaining the time unit. The data may remain visible, but the comparison description exposes an internal missing-value word.
